name: Closed vs open foot track (shadow)
why: Safety-relevant: a closed track must not be read as open. In the current web style the only difference is the colour of a 40%-opacity shadow.

name: Contour vs state highway
why: Both orange-family; distinguished mainly by width and casing.

name: Contour vs pipeline
why: Two thin lines that can run across slopes.

name: Contour vs vegetation edge
why: Thin lines that cross frequently; the classic orange/green deutan confusion.

name: Hot vs cold spring
why: Same glyph, colour-only distinction (check: symbol may also differ).

name: Historic site vs hut label
why: Red vs near-black text; red is the classic protan/red-light failure.

name: Scrub vs scattered scrub
why: Travel-relevant: scrub vs scattered scrub changes route choice.

name: Scrub vs water
why: Pale green vs pale blue — the tritan / ageing-lens axis.

name: Water label vs peak label
why: Label class is signalled by colour (+ italic for water).

name: Contour vs white (visibility)
why: Can a 0.4–0.6px contour be seen at all? WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 for graphical objects.
